title: Remove pin bones from a salmon fillet
instruction: Use the fishbone tweezers to remove all four pin bones from the salmon fillet and put them in the waste dish. Keep the flesh intact.
context: Preparing fish requires gripping fine bones and pulling along their direction without tearing the soft flesh.
setup: A chilled (2–5 °C), skin-on Atlantic salmon portion, nominally 150 × 90 × 25 mm, with four natural pin bones remaining. It lies on a 280 × 260 × 12 mm wooden board beside a 90 mm waste dish. Both arms have mounted stainless fishbone tweezer leaves, 140 mm long with 40 × 6 × 1 mm working ends and 4 N actuator limits. Bone tips protrude 3–5 mm; the fixed layout and specimen preparation are in README. Disposable gripper sleeves and a washable table mat protect the rig in real trials; only the washable steel tool ends touch food.
scoring: After both hands stay 50 mm clear for 3 seconds, award 0.25 per whole bone fully removed and entirely inside the upright waste dish. Any broken bone, retained broken-bone fragment ≥3 mm, flesh piece ≥5 mm detached, or tear extending an entry opening by ≥5 mm scores 0. The fillet must remain on its board and the dish upright within 15°. Use photographs, a ruler, video and post-trial inspection of the four entry sites. Other outcomes score 0.
fidelity: Yielding flesh sectors and bending, breakable bones approximate the food. A finite directional sliding resistance represents embedded tissue and ends after extraction; bone/flesh contacts then resume. The visible surface follows sector motion and separates after damage. Mounted parallel jaws approximate held fish tweezers; a contact-gated native pinch slips at finite load. Material values are uncalibrated; no task-object poses are assigned during execution.
reset_notes: Use a new chilled, unpinboned portion each real trial; keep four spaced natural bones and remove the others beforehand. Restore the photographed layout. Trial food is not served.
